question: Which of the following have mountain range young fold mountains?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The Alps mountain range** is classified as a** young fold mountain range.**
 
• The formation of the **Alps **began about 65 million years ago during the** Paleogene period **and continued into the **Neogene period**, which ended about** 2.6 million** years ago.
 
• The range was formed by the collision of the** African and Eurasian tectonic plates**, which caused the** Earth's crust to buckle and fold, forming the Alps.**
 
• The **ongoing collision** between these two plates is still causing the Alps to rise by abou**t 1-2 millimeters per year.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Appalachian Mountains **are a mountain range that stretches from** Canada to Alabama in the United States**.

 
 
• They are part of the **Appalachian Mountain system, **which includes a series of **smaller ranges and valleys**.
 
• The mountains were formed over **480 million years **ago during the Ordovician period, and they have been eroded and reshaped by various geological processes over time.
 
 
 
• **The Aravalli Mountain Range** is a range of mountains located in western India, stretching **approximately 800 km** from **northeast to southwest across the Indian states of Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat.**
 
 
• The range starts from **Delhi **and passes through** southern Haryana, through Rajasthan and ends in Gujarat.**
 
• The **highest peak **of the range is** Guru Shikhar, located in Mount Abu, Rajasthan, with an elevation of 1,722 meters above sea level.**
 
• **The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, estimated to be around 350 million years old.**
 
• The range is known for its rich biodiversity and is home to a number of** wildlife species, including leopards, hyenas, jackals, and various species of birds and reptiles.**
 
 
 
• **​The Ural Mountains, also known as the Urals, are a mountain range located in western Russia, running north-south from the Arctic Ocean to the Ural River and northwestern Kazakhstan. **
 
 
• **The range forms the natural boundary between Europe and Asia, and its highest peak is Mount Narodnaya, which rises to an elevation of 1,894 meters (6,214 feet).**
 
• **The Ural Mountains are rich in minerals, including iron ore, copper, nickel, and coal, and have been an important mining region since the 18th century. **
 
• **The region is also home to many indigenous peoples, including the Mansi, Khanty, and Nenets, who have a rich culture and traditional way of life that has been threatened by industrialization and resource extraction.**
